place.en: The hidden realm · Below the drop

setup.zh: 别人都往右，你往左，往下。崖底是一面光秃秃的石墙——墙后头，有风。
setup.en: Everyone goes right; you go left, and down. At the foot of the cliff, a bare stone wall — and behind it, wind.

recap.zh: 秘境里，银月领着你往左、往下；墙后头有风，墙上刻着九宫——五居中央，墙开了。
recap.en: In the hidden realm Yinyue led you left and down; there was a draught behind the wall, the nine squares carved on it — five in the middle, and the wall opened.

en: "…This place. I have been here before."

label.en: The nine squares on the wall

text.zh: 九个格子，三三一排，边角给水泡得发白，正中那一格，比别的磨得都亮。
text.en: Nine squares, three by three, their edges bleached by water. The middle one is worn brighter than the rest.

text.zh: 石块一共九块，点子从一到九，一块不少，只是都给水泡得发黑。
text.en: Nine stones in all, dotted one to nine, not one missing — all of them blackened by the water.

text.zh: 风是暖的，带着一股土腥气，从最底下那道缝里一丝一丝透出来。
text.en: The draught is warm and smells of earth; it seeps thread by thread from the lowest crack.

story.zh:
走进石门的那一刻，他胸口的木牌「腾」地一烫。

那一烫，跟往常不同。往常烫一下，是它醒了，有话要说；这一回烫了一下，没有停，第二下，第三下，一下紧似一下，倒像是一颗心在他胸口底下跳，跳得越来越急。他把木牌从衣领里掏出来，只见那条银色的尾巴亮得刺眼，亮得他手心都照白了。

一只半透明的小银狐从木牌里钻了出来，蹲在他肩膀上。这一回，它的身子比从前实了些，没那么透了，月光底下能照过去的地方，如今只照得过一半。它没有打哈欠，也没有骂他吵，一双金色的眼睛睁得大大的，四下里慢慢地看，看石壁，看石壁上的花纹，看脚底下的石板，鼻子一抽一抽的，像在闻着什么很远、很远的东西。

它开口了，声音却变了，不是往常那个又困又不耐烦的妖王，倒像一个人站在自己小时候住过的院子里：「……这地方。本王来过。」

小满问：「什么时候？」

银月道：「不知道。」

小满问：「来做什么？」

银月道：「不知道。」

小满道：「那你知道什么？」

银月的鼻子又抽了一抽，隔了很久，才道：「……往左。」

地图上画的路，是往右的。三百多个人进了门，便顺着长廊往右走，一路上呼朋引伴，叮叮当当，声音在石壁上撞来撞去，撞成一片。往左，是一道窄窄的石缝，缝口给一块塌下来的大石头堵了一半，石头上刻着一个歪歪扭扭的「凶」字，字底下画了个骷髅头，骷髅头的眼眶里，还有人拿炭添了两道眼泪。

地图上，这道石缝旁边，也有一行小字：「左崖，粘人。十年前粘住三个，粘了三天，出来疯了一个。」

小满看着那行小字，看了一会儿，把地图折好，揣进怀里，侧着身子，从那半边石缝里挤了进去。

石缝后头是一段往下走的石阶，窄，陡，湿，石阶上长满了青苔，踩上去滑溜溜的。走了约莫一顿饭的工夫，石阶到了头，前面是一道断崖。崖下黑洞洞的，看不见底，只听得见底下有水滴的声音，一滴，隔很久，又一滴。

银月道：「往下。」

小满趴在崖边往下看了看，道：「下面什么都没有。」

银月道：「往下。」

小满道：「你怎么知道下面有东西？」

银月道：「本王不知道下面有东西。本王知道，这里的灵气是从下面上来的。」它顿了一顿，声音低了下去，「……很厚的灵气。外头那条河，那座山，那间讲堂，本王睡着的时候都闻过，薄得像一碗刷锅水。这里的……像一口封了几百年的井，刚揭开盖子。」

小满想起了褚先生望着泗水的那双眼睛。他没有再问，把袖子挽了起来，顺着崖壁往下爬。

他是猎户家的孩子，爬崖是本行。蒙山上的崖，比这陡的多的是。可爬到一半，他便觉出这道崖跟蒙山的不一样。蒙山的崖是活的，石缝里长草，草根底下有土，土里有虫，手抓上去，石头是凉的，却凉得有个分寸。这道崖却是死的，从上到下，一根草也不长，石头凉得透骨，凉得像是从来没有晒过一天日头。他爬几尺，便停一停，把手放在嘴边呵一口气，再往下爬。

爬到底，是一片平地，平地尽头，是一面石墙。

那石墙光秃秃的，平平整整，一丈来高，两丈来宽，不见门，不见缝，不见花纹，就是一面墙。墙脚下，东一块西一块地堆着些石头，大大小小，有方有圆，像是从崖上滚下来的。

小满在墙前站了很久，道：「什么都没有。」

银月道：「那面墙后头，有风。」

小满道：「墙后头怎么会有风？」

银月道：「你看。」

小满便看。他从头上拔下一根头发——这一回他学乖了，离银月远远的——捏在手指头上，举到墙前头。那根头发起先软塌塌地垂着，垂了好一会儿，然后，很轻很轻地，往墙的方向飘了一飘。又一飘。飘得很慢，却一次比一次坚决，倒像墙那边有一张嘴，隔着一层石头，在慢慢地吸气。

小满看着那根头发，心里咯噔一下。他蹲下身来，把手贴在墙上，从左往右，一寸一寸地摸过去。石头是凉的，处处都凉，可凉得不一样。他爹教过他摸兽迹：同是一块泥，踩过的和没踩过的，手摸上去不一样；踩过一天的和踩过三天的，又不一样。他摸了一遍，又摸一遍，摸到第三遍，在墙的右下角，摸着了一块石头，比旁边的更凉，凉得发麻，四边还有一道极细极细的缝，细得指甲都塞不进去。
story.en:
The moment he stepped through the stone door, the token on his chest flared hot.

That flare was not like the others. Other times it flared once — it was awake and had something to say; this time it flared and did not stop — a second time, a third, each quicker than the last, as if a heart were beating under his chest, faster and faster. He pulled the token from his collar: the silver tail on it blazed so bright his palm went white.

A half-transparent little silver fox slipped out of the token and sat on his shoulder. This time its body was more solid than before, not so see-through — where once moonlight passed through all of it, now only half. It didn't yawn, didn't scold him for noise; its golden eyes were wide open, looking slowly all round — at the rock walls, the patterns on them, the flagstones underfoot — its nose twitching as if at something very, very far away.

It spoke, but its voice had changed — not the sleepy, impatient demon queen, more like someone standing in the courtyard where they lived as a child: "…This place. I've been here."

"When?" Xiaoman asked.

"Don't know," said Yinyue.

"What for?"

"Don't know."

"Then what do you know?"

Yinyue's nose twitched again, and after a long while it said: "…Left."

The road on the map went right. Three hundred and more had come through the door and gone right along the long gallery, calling to friends, clattering, the noise banging off the rock walls into one din. To the left was a narrow crack in the rock, half blocked by a great fallen stone; on the stone someone had carved a crooked "凶" — ill-omen — and a skull under it, and into the skull's eye sockets someone had added two tears in charcoal.

On the map, beside this crack, was a line of small writing too: "Left cliff — sticky. Ten years ago it stuck three, stuck them three days; one came out mad."

Xiaoman looked at that line a while, folded the map, put it in his coat, turned sideways, and squeezed through the half-crack.

Beyond it a flight of stone steps went down — narrow, steep, wet, grown over with moss, slick underfoot. After about the time of a meal the steps ended, and ahead was a sheer drop. Below, pitch dark, no bottom to be seen; only the sound of water dripping far down — one drop, a long pause, another.

"Down," said Yinyue.

Xiaoman lay at the edge and looked. "There's nothing down there."

"Down."

"How do you know there's something down there?"

"I don't know there's something down there. I know the spirit qi here comes up from below." It paused, and its voice sank. "…Thick qi. That river outside, that mountain, that lecture hall — I smelled them all in my sleep, thin as dishwater. This… is like a well sealed a few hundred years, the lid just lifted."

Xiaoman thought of Master Chu's eyes as he looked at the Si. He asked no more, rolled up his sleeves, and climbed down the cliff.

He was a hunter's son; climbing cliffs was his trade. Meng Mountain had plenty steeper than this. But halfway down he felt this cliff was not like Meng Mountain's. Meng Mountain's cliffs were alive — grass in the cracks, soil under the grass, bugs in the soil; grip the rock and it was cold, but cold within measure. This cliff was dead: top to bottom not a blade of grass, the rock cold to the bone, as if it had never had one day of sun. Every few feet he stopped and breathed on his hands, then climbed on.

At the bottom was a flat space, and at the end of the flat space, a stone wall.

The wall was bare and smooth, ten feet high and twenty wide — no door, no crack, no pattern: a wall. At its foot lay stones scattered here and there, big and small, square and round, as if they had rolled down from the cliff.

Xiaoman stood before the wall a long time. "There's nothing."

"Behind that wall," said Yinyue, "there's wind."

"How can there be wind behind a wall?"

"Look."

So Xiaoman looked. He pulled a hair from his head — he'd learned this time, and held it well away from Yinyue — pinched it between his fingers and held it up before the wall. At first the hair hung limp, a good while; then, very, very lightly, it drifted toward the wall. And again. Slowly, but more decided each time, as if on the other side of the wall there were a mouth, breathing in slowly through a layer of stone.

Watching the hair, Xiaoman's heart gave a jolt. He crouched, laid his hand on the wall, and felt his way from left to right an inch at a time. The stone was cold, cold everywhere, but not all cold alike. His father had taught him to feel for tracks: the same mud feels different trodden and untrodden; trodden one day and trodden three, different again. He went over it once, twice, and on the third pass, at the lower right corner of the wall, he found a stone colder than those beside it, cold enough to numb, with a seam round its edges so fine a fingernail wouldn't go in.

exits.means: has solved the nine squares and goes through the wall

refuse.zh: 九个格子还没填对。墙不动。
refuse.en: The nine squares are not right yet. The wall does not move.

story.zh:
他按了下去。

只听得「轰隆隆——」一阵闷响，从墙根底下一直响到崖顶上，震得崖壁上的碎石子簌簌地往下掉。那面墙从正中裂开了一道缝，缝越来越宽，越来越宽，一股风从缝里涌了出来，扑在他脸上。那风是暖的，暖得像春天，带着一股味道，小满这辈子从没闻过，说不上是什么，只觉得一闻，心里便静了。
story.en:
He pressed.

A long, dull rumble — "*rrrrumble*" — ran from the foot of the wall up to the top of the cliff, shaking loose pebbles that pattered down the rock. The wall split down the middle; the crack widened and widened, and a wind poured out of it into his face. The wind was warm, warm as spring, and carried a smell Xiaoman had never smelled in his life — he couldn't say what — only that one breath of it and his heart went still.
